drivingQuestion: Is the evening prayer obligatory or optional — and what followed when Rabban Gamliel forced Rabbi Yehoshua to stand for having ruled otherwise?
outcomeNote: Rabban Gamliel is deposed, R' Elazar ben Azarya installed, the two are reconciled, and a rota of three weeks to one restores Rabban Gamliel without demoting his successor; the halakhic question of the evening prayer itself is left standing as the Abaye–Rava dispute of 27b.14.

segments.he: כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר, תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר חוֹבָה, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר רְשׁוּת. אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר חוֹבָה. וְרָבָא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר רְשׁוּת.
segments.en: It is «in accordance with» the opinion of «the one who said: The evening prayer is optional.» As «Rav Yehuda said» that «Shmuel said» with regard to «the evening prayer. Rabban Gamliel says:» It is «obligatory. Rabbi Yehoshua says:» It is «optional. Abaye said: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the one who said:» The evening prayer is «obligatory. Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with the statement of the one who said:» The evening prayer is «optional.»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ. אָמַר לוֹ: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת אוֹ חוֹבָה? אָמַר לֵיהּ: רְשׁוּת.
segments.en: «The Sages taught:» There was «an incident involving a student, who came before Rabbi Yehoshua.» The student «said to him: Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?» Rabbi Yehoshua «said to him: Optional.»

segments.he: בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אָמַר לוֹ: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת אוֹ חוֹבָה? אָמַר לוֹ: חוֹבָה. אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לִי רְשׁוּת?! אָמַר לוֹ: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיִּכָּנְסוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
segments.en: The same student «came before Rabban Gamliel and said to him: Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?» Rabban Gamliel «said to him: Obligatory.» The student «said to» Rabban Gamliel: «But didn’t Rabbi Yehoshua tell me» that the evening prayer is «optional?» Rabban Gamliel «said to» the student: «Wait until the “masters of the shields,”» a reference to the Torah scholars who battle in the war of Torah, «enter the study hall,» at which point we will discuss this issue.

segments.he: כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין, עָמַד הַשּׁוֹאֵל וְשָׁאַל: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת אוֹ חוֹבָה? אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: חוֹבָה. אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁחוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה? אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לָאו. אָמַר לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא מִשִּׁמְךָ אָמְרוּ לִי רְשׁוּת!
segments.en: «When the masters of the shields entered, the questioner stood» before everyone present «and asked: Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory? Rabban Gamliel said to him: Obligatory.» In order to ascertain whether or not Rabbi Yehoshua still maintained his opinion, «Rabban Gamliel said to» the Sages: «Is there any person who disputes this matter? Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No,» no one disagrees. In deference to the Nasi, he did not wish to argue with him publicly (Tziyyun LeNefesh Ḥayya). Rabban Gamliel «said to» Rabbi Yehoshua: «But was it not in your name that they told me» that the evening prayer is «optional?»

segments.he: אָמַר לֵיהּ: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, עֲמוֹד עַל רַגְלֶיךָ וְיָעִידוּ בְּךָ. עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר אִלְמָלֵא אֲנִי חַי וְהוּא מֵת — יָכוֹל הַחַי לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַמֵּת. וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁאֲנִי חַי וְהוּא חַי — הֵיאַךְ יָכוֹל הַחַי לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי?
segments.en: Rabban Gamliel «said to» Rabbi Yehoshua: «Yehoshua, stand on your feet and they will testify against you. Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said: If I were alive and» the student «were dead, the living can contradict the dead,» and I could deny issuing that ruling. «Now that I am alive and he is alive, how can the living contradict the living?» I have no choice but to admit that I said it.

segments.he: הָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עוֹמֵד עַל רַגְלָיו, עַד שֶׁרִנְּנוּ כׇּל הָעָם וְאָמְרוּ לְחוּצְפִּית הַתּוּרְגְּמָן: עֲמוֹד! וְעָמַד.
segments.en: In the meantime, «Rabban Gamliel,» as the Nasi, «was sitting and lecturing, and Rabbi Yehoshua» all the while «was standing on his feet,» because Rabban Gamliel did not instruct him to sit. He remained standing in deference to the Nasi. This continued for some time, «until» it aroused great resentment against Rabban Gamliel, and «all of the people» assembled began «murmuring and said to Ḥutzpit the disseminator: Stop» conveying Rabban Gamliel’s lecture. «And he stopped.»

segments.he: אָמְרִי: עַד כַּמָּה נְצַעֲרֵיהּ וְנֵיזִיל, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה אֶשְׁתָּקַד צַעֲרֵיהּ. בִּבְכוֹרוֹת בְּמַעֲשֵׂה דְרַבִּי צָדוֹק צַעֲרֵיהּ. הָכָא נָמֵי צַעֲרֵיהּ, תָּא וְנַעְבְּרֵיהּ!
segments.en: The Gemara relates that in their murmuring «they said: How long will» Rabban Gamliel «continue afflicting him? Last year on Rosh HaShana, he afflicted him;» Rabban Gamliel ordered Rabbi Yehoshua to come to him carrying his staff and bag, on the day on which Yom Kippur occurred, according to Rabbi Yehoshua’s calculations. «Regarding the firstborn, in the incident» involving the question «of Rabbi Tzadok, he afflicted him» just as he did now, and forced him to remain standing as punishment for his failure to defend his differing opinion. «Here too, he is afflicting him. Let us remove him» from his position as Nasi.

segments.he: מַאן נוֹקֵים לֵיהּ? נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ — בַּעַל מַעֲשֶׂה הוּא. נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — דִּילְמָא עָנֵישׁ לֵיהּ, דְּלֵית לֵיהּ זְכוּת אָבוֹת.
segments.en: It was so agreed, but the question arose: «Whom shall we establish» in his place? Shall we «establish Rabbi Yehoshua» in his place? The Sages rejected that option because Rabbi Yehoshua «was party to the incident» for which Rabban Gamliel was deposed. Appointing him would be extremely upsetting for Rabban Gamliel. Shall we «establish Rabbi Akiva» in his place? The Sages rejected that option because Rabbi Akiva, who descended from a family of converts, would be vulnerable. «Perhaps» due to Rabban Gamliel’s resentment he «would» cause «him» to be divinely «punished as he lacks the merit of his ancestors» to protect him.

segments.he: אֶלָּא נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, דְּהוּא חָכָם, וְהוּא עָשִׁיר, וְהוּא עֲשִׂירִי לְעֶזְרָא. הוּא חָכָם — דְּאִי מַקְשֵׁי לֵיהּ, מְפָרֵק לֵיהּ. וְהוּא עָשִׁיר — דְּאִי אִית לֵיהּ לְפַלּוֹחֵי לְבֵי קֵיסָר, אַף הוּא אָזֵל וּפָלַח. וְהוּא עֲשִׂירִי לְעֶזְרָא — דְּאִית לֵיהּ זְכוּת אָבוֹת, וְלָא מָצֵי עָנֵישׁ לֵיהּ. אֲתוֹ וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: נִיחָא לֵיהּ לְמָר דְּלֶיהְוֵי רֵישׁ מְתִיבְתָּא? אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֵיזִיל וְאִימְּלִיךְ בְּאִינָשֵׁי בֵּיתִי. אֲזַל וְאִמְּלִיךְ בִּדְבֵיתְהוּ. אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ:
segments.en: «Rather,» suggested the Sages, «let us establish Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya» in his place, his outstanding characteristics set him apart from the other candidates. «He is wise, rich, and a tenth» generation descendant «of Ezra.» The Gemara explains: «He is wise, so if» Rabban Gamliel raises a «challenge» in matters of Torah, «he will answer it» and not be embarrassed. «And he is rich, so if the need» arises «to pay homage to the Caesar’s court» and serve as a representative of Israel to lobby and negotiate, he has sufficient wealth to cover the costs of the long journeys, taxes, and gifts, so «he too is able to go and pay homage. And he is» a «tenth» generation descendant «of Ezra, so he has the merit of his ancestors, and» Rabban Gamliel «will be unable to» cause «him» to be «punished. They came and said to him: Would the Master consent to being the Head of the Yeshiva? He said to them: I will go and consult with my household. He went and consulted with his wife. She said to him:»

segments.he: דִּלְמָא מְעַבְּרִין לָךְ. אֲמַר לַהּ: לִשְׁתַּמַּשׁ אִינָשׁ יוֹמָא חֲדָא בְּכָסָא דְמוֹקְרָא, וְלִמְחַר לִיתְּבַר. אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: לֵית לָךָ חִיוָּרָתָא. הָהוּא יוֹמָא בַּר תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי שְׁנֵי הֲוָה, אִתְרְחִישׁ לֵיהּ נִיסָּא וְאִהַדַּרוּ לֵיהּ תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי דָּרֵי חִיוָּרָתָא. הַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: הֲרֵי אֲנִי כְּבֶן שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה. וְלֹא ״בֶּן שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה״.
segments.en: There is room for concern. «Perhaps they will remove you» from office just as they removed Rabban Gamliel. «He said to her,» based on the folk saying: «Let a person use an expensive goblet one day and let it break tomorrow.» In other words, one should take advantage of an opportunity that presents itself and he need not concern himself whether or not it will last. «She said to him: You have no white» hair, and it is inappropriate for one so young to head the Sages. The Gemara relates: «That day, he was eighteen years old, a miracle transpired for him and eighteen rows of hair turned white.» The Gemara comments: «That» explains «that which Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said: I am as one who is seventy years old and he did not say: I am seventy years old,» because he looked older than he actually was.

segments.he: תָּנָא אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם, סִלְּקוּהוּ לְשׁוֹמֵר הַפֶּתַח וְנִתְּנָה לָהֶם רְשׁוּת לַתַּלְמִידִים לִיכָּנֵס. שֶׁהָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַכְרִיז וְאוֹמֵר: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד שֶׁאֵין תּוֹכוֹ כְּבָרוֹ, לֹא יִכָּנֵס לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ.
segments.en: «It was taught: On that day» that they removed Rabban Gamliel from his position and appointed Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya in his place, there was also a fundamental change in the general approach of the study hall as «they dismissed the guard at the door and permission was granted to the students to enter.» Instead of Rabban Gamliel’s selective approach that asserted that the students must be screened before accepting them into the study hall, the new approach asserted that anyone who seeks to study should be given opportunity to do so. «As Rabban Gamliel would proclaim and say: Any student whose inside,» his thoughts and feelings, «are not like his outside,» i.e., his conduct and his character traits are lacking, «will not enter the study hall.»

segments.he: הַהוּא יוֹמָא אִתּוֹסְפוּ כַּמָּה סַפְסַלֵּי. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵף בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן. חַד אָמַר: אִתּוֹסְפוּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה סַפְסַלֵּי. וְחַד אָמַר: שְׁבַע מְאָה סַפְסַלֵּי. הֲוָה קָא חָלְשָׁה דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, אֲמַר: דִּלְמָא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מָנַעְתִּי תּוֹרָה מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל. אַחְזוֹ לֵיהּ בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ חַצְבֵי חִיוָּרֵי דְּמַלְיִין קִטְמָא. וְלָא הִיא, הַהִיא לְיַתּוֹבֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ, הוּא דְּאַחְזוֹ לֵיהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «On that day several benches were added» to the study hall to accommodate the numerous students. «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Abba Yosef ben Dostai and the Rabbis disputed this» matter. «One said: Four hundred benches were added» to the study hall. «And one said: Seven hundred benches were added» to the study hall. When he saw the tremendous growth in the number of students, «Rabban Gamliel was disheartened. He said: Perhaps, Heaven forbid, I prevented Israel from» engaging in «Torah» study. «They showed him in his dream white jugs filled with ashes» alluding to the fact that the additional students were worthless idlers. The Gemara comments: «That is not» the case, but «that» dream «was shown to him to ease his mind» so that he would not feel bad.

segments.he: תָּנָא: עֵדֻיוֹת בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם נִשְׁנֵית. וְכׇל הֵיכָא דְּאָמְרִינַן ״בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם״, הַהוּא יוֹמָא הֲוָה. וְלֹא הָיְתָה הֲלָכָה שֶׁהָיְתָה תְּלוּיָה בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ שֶׁלֹּא פֵּירְשׁוּהָ. וְאַף רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לֹא מָנַע עַצְמוֹ מִבֵּית הַמִּדְרָשׁ אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
segments.en: «It was taught:» There is a tradition that tractate «Eduyyot was taught that day. And everywhere» in the Mishna or in a baraita «that they say: On that day, it is» referring to «that day. There was no halakha whose ruling was pending in the study hall that they did not explain» and arrive at a practical halakhic conclusion. «And even Rabban Gamliel did not avoid the study hall for even one moment,» as he held no grudge against those who removed him from office and he participated in the halakhic discourse in the study hall as one of the Sages.

segments.he: דִּתְנַן: בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם בָּא יְהוּדָה גֵּר עַמּוֹנִי לִפְנֵיהֶם בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ. אָמַר לָהֶם: מָה אֲנִי לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל?
segments.en: «As we learned» in a mishna: «On that day, Yehuda, the Ammonite convert, came before» the students in the study hall «and he said to them: What is my» legal status in terms of «entering into the congregation» of Israel, i.e., to marry a Jewish woman?

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: אָסוּר אַתָּה לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מוּתָּר אַתָּה לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל. אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא יָבֹא עַמּוֹנִי וּמוֹאָבִי בִּקְהַל ה׳״? אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וְכִי עַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב בִּמְקוֹמָן הֵן יוֹשְׁבִין? כְּבָר עָלָה סַנְחֵרִיב מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר וּבִלְבֵּל אֶת כׇּל הָאוּמּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְאָסִיר גְּבֻלוֹת עַמִּים וַעֲתוּדוֹתֵיהֶם שׁוֹשֵׂתִי וְאוֹרִיד כַּבִּיר יוֹשְׁבִים״, וְכׇל דְּפָרֵישׁ — מֵרוּבָּא פָּרֵישׁ.
segments.en: «Rabban Gamliel said to him: You are forbidden to enter into the congregation. Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: You are permitted to enter into the congregation. Rabban Gamliel said to» Rabbi Yehoshua: «Wasn’t it already stated: “An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord;» even to the tenth generation shall none of them enter into the congregation of the Lord forever” (Deuteronomy 23:4)? How can you permit him to enter the congregation? «Rabbi Yehoshua said to» Rabban Gamliel: «Do Ammon and Moab reside in their place? Sennacherib already came and,» through his policy of population transfer, «scrambled all the nations» and settled other nations in place of Ammon. Consequently, the current residents of Ammon and Moab are not ethnic Ammonites and Moabites, «as it is stated in» reference to Sennacherib: «“I have removed the bounds of the peoples, and have robbed their treasures, and have brought down as one mighty the inhabitants”» (Isaiah 10:13). «And» although it is conceivable that this particular convert is an ethnic Ammonite, nevertheless, there is no need for concern due to the halakhic principle: «Anything that parts» from a group «parts from the majority,» and the assumption is that he is from the majority of nations whose members are permitted to enter the congregation.

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן אָשִׁיב אֶת שְׁבוּת בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן נְאֻם ה׳״, וּכְבָר שָׁבוּ!
segments.en: «Rabban Gamliel said to» Rabbi Yehoshua: «But wasn’t it already stated: “But afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon, says the Lord”» (Jeremiah 49:6) «and they have already returned» to their land? Therefore, he is an ethnic Ammonite and he may not convert.

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר ״וְשַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁבוּת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וַעֲדַיִין לֹא שָׁבוּ. מִיָּד הִתִּירוּהוּ לָבֹא בַּקָּהָל.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehoshua said to» Rabban Gamliel: That is no proof. «Wasn’t it already stated» in another prophecy: «“And I will turn the captivity of My people Israel» and they shall build the waste cities, and inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, and drink the wine thereof; they shall also make gardens, and eat the fruit of them” (Amos 9:14), «and they have not yet returned?» In rendering the ruling, only proven facts may be taken into consideration. «They immediately permitted him to enter the congregation.» This proves that Rabban Gamliel did not absent himself from the study hall that day and participated in the halakhic discourse.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: הוֹאִיל וְהָכִי הֲוָה, אֵיזִיל וַאֲפַיְּיסֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ. כִּי מְטָא לְבֵיתֵיהּ, חֲזִינְהוּ לְאַשְׁיָתָא דְבֵיתֵיהּ דְּמַשְׁחֲרָן. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִכּוֹתְלֵי בֵיתְךָ אַתָּה נִיכָּר שֶׁפֶּחָמִי אַתָּה. אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹי לוֹ לַדּוֹר שֶׁאַתָּה פַּרְנָסוֹ, שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ בְּצַעֲרָן שֶׁל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, בַּמֶּה הֵם מִתְפַּרְנְסִים וּבַמֶּה הֵם נִזּוֹנִים.
segments.en: «Rabban Gamliel said» to himself: «Since this is» the situation, that the people are following Rabbi Yehoshua, apparently he was right. Therefore, it would be appropriate for me to «go and appease Rabbi Yehoshua. When he reached» Rabbi Yehoshua’s «house, he saw» that «the walls of his house were black.» Rabban Gamliel «said to» Rabbi Yehoshua in wonderment: «From the walls of your house it is apparent that you are a blacksmith,» as until then he had no idea that Rabbi Yehoshua was forced to engage in that arduous trade in order to make a living. Rabbi Yehoshua «said to him: Woe unto a generation that you are its leader as you are unaware of the difficulties of Torah scholars, how they make a living and how they feed themselves.»

segments.he: אָמַר לוֹ: נַעֲנֵיתִי לְךָ מְחוֹל לִי. לָא אַשְׁגַּח בֵּיהּ: עֲשֵׂה בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹד אַבָּא. פַּיֵּיס.
segments.en: Rabban Gamliel «said to him: I insulted you, forgive me.» Rabbi Yehoshua «paid him no attention» and did not forgive him. He asked him again: «Do it in deference to my father,» Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who was one of the leaders of Israel at the time of the destruction of the Temple. «He was appeased.»

segments.he: אֲמַרוּ: מַאן נֵיזִיל וְלֵימָא לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן. אֲמַר לְהוּ הַהוּא כּוֹבֵס: אֲנָא אָזֵילְנָא. שְׁלַח לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא: מַאן דְּלָבֵישׁ מַדָּא — יִלְבַּשׁ מַדָּא, וּמַאן דְּלָא לָבֵישׁ מַדָּא יֵימַר לֵיהּ לְמַאן דְּלָבֵישׁ מַדָּא: שְׁלַח מַדָּךְ וַאֲנָא אֶלְבְּשֵׁיהּ?! אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְרַבָּנַן: טְרוּקוּ גַּלֵּי דְּלָא לֵיתוּ עַבְדֵי דְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וּלְצַעֲרוּ לְרַבָּנַן.
segments.en: Now that Rabbi Yehoshua was no longer offended, it was only natural that Rabban Gamliel would be restored to his position. «They said: Who will go and inform the Sages?» Apparently, they were not eager to carry out the mission that would undo the previous actions and remove Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya from his position as Nasi. «This launderer said to them: I will go. Rabbi Yehoshua sent to» the Sages «to the study hall: The one who wears the uniform will» continue to «wear the uniform,» the original Nasi will remain in his position so that «the one who did not wear the uniform will» not «say to the one who wears the uniform, remove your uniform and I will wear it.» Apparently, the Sages believed that this emissary was dispatched at the initiative of Rabban Gamliel and they ignored him. «Rabbi Akiva said to the Sages: Lock the gates so that Rabban Gamliel’s servants will not come and disturb the Sages.»

segments.he: אֲמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: מוּטָב דְּאֵיקוּם וְאֵיזִיל אֲנָא לְגַבַּיְיהוּ. אֲתָא טְרַף אַבָּבָא. אֲמַר לְהוּ: מַזֶּה בֶּן מַזֶּה יַזֶּה. וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא מַזֶּה וְלֹא בֶּן מַזֶּה יֹאמַר לְמַזֶּה בֶּן מַזֶּה מֵימֶיךָ מֵי מְעָרָה וְאֶפְרְךָ אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה. אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, נִתְפַּיַּיסְתָּ? כְּלוּם עָשִׂינוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל כְּבוֹדְךָ, לְמָחָר אֲנִי וְאַתָּה נַשְׁכִּים לְפִתְחוֹ.
segments.en: When he heard what happened, «Rabbi Yehoshua said: It is best if I go to them. He came and knocked on the door. He said to them» with a slight variation: «One who sprinkles» pure water on those who are ritually impure, «son of one who sprinkles» water «shall» continue «to sprinkle» water. And it is inappropriate that he who is «neither one who sprinkles nor son of one who sprinkles will say to one who sprinkles son of one who sprinkles: Your water is cave water» and not the running water required to purify one exposed to ritual impurity imparted by a corpse «and your ashes are burnt ashes» and not the ashes of a red heifer. «Rabbi Akiva said to him: Rabbi Yehoshua, have you been appeased? Everything we did was to» defend «your honor.» If you have forgiven him, none of us is opposed. «Early tomorrow you and I will go to» Rabban Gamliel’s «doorway» and offer to restore him to his position as Nasi.

segments.he: אָמְרִי: הֵיכִי נַעֲבֵיד, נַעְבְּרֵיהּ — גְּמִירִי מַעֲלִין בַּקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵין מוֹרִידִין. נִדְרוֹשׁ מָר חֲדָא שַׁבְּתָא וּמַר חֲדָא שַׁבְּתָא — אָתֵי לְקַנּאוֹיֵי. אֶלָּא: לִדְרוֹשׁ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל תְּלָתָא שַׁבָּתֵי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה חֲדָא שַׁבְּתָא. וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר מָר שַׁבָּת שֶׁל מִי הָיְתָה — שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הָיְתָה. וְאוֹתוֹ תַּלְמִיד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי הֲוָה.
segments.en: The question arose what to do with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya? «They said: What shall we do? Remove him» from his position. That is inappropriate as we «learned» a halakha through tradition: One «elevates» to a higher level of «sanctity and does not downgrade.» Therefore, one who was the Nasi of the Sanhedrin cannot be demoted. «Let» one «Sage lecture one week and» the other «Sage one week, they will come to be jealous» one of another, as they will be forced to appoint one as the acting head of the Sanhedrin. «Rather, Rabban Gamliel will lecture three weeks and Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya» will lecture as head of the yeshiva «one week.» That arrangement was adopted «and that is» the explanation of the exchange in tractate Ḥagiga: «Whose week was it? It was the week of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.» One final detail: «That student» who asked the original question that sparked this entire incident «was Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai.»

moves.summary: The Gemara aligns the preceding ruling with the view that the evening prayer is optional.
moves.about: the preceding ruling is aligned with the view that the evening prayer is optional, which the sugya at once attributes to R' Yehoshua

moves.summary: Rav Yehuda cites Shmuel that Rabban Gamliel held the evening prayer obligatory and R' Yehoshua optional.
moves.about: the tannaitic dispute between Rabban Gamliel and R' Yehoshua over the evening prayer

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: הלכה כדברי האומר חובה
moves.summary: Abaye rules the halakha follows the view that it is obligatory.
moves.about: the halakha follows the one who holds the evening prayer obligatory, i.e. Rabban Gamliel

moves.cueHe: ורבא אמר: הלכה כדברי האומר רשות
moves.summary: Rava rules the opposite: the halakha follows the view that it is optional.
moves.about: the halakha follows the one who holds the evening prayer optional, i.e. R' Yehoshua

moves.summary: A baraita is brought recounting the incident behind the tannaitic dispute.
moves.about: a baraita recounting the incident that lay behind the tannaitic dispute

moves.cueHe: אמר לו: תפלת ערבית רשות או חובה?
moves.summary: A student asks R' Yehoshua whether the evening prayer is optional or obligatory.
moves.about: whether the evening prayer is optional or obligatory

moves.summary: R' Yehoshua answers: optional.
moves.about: the evening prayer is optional

moves.cueHe: בא לפני רבן גמליאל, אמר לו
moves.summary: The student puts the same question to Rabban Gamliel.
moves.about: whether the evening prayer is optional or obligatory

moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel answers: obligatory.
moves.about: the evening prayer is obligatory

moves.cueHe: והלא רבי יהושע אמר לי רשות?!
moves.summary: The student sets Rabban Gamliel's ruling against R' Yehoshua's.
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel's ruling that the evening prayer is obligatory conflicts with the ruling R' Yehoshua gave the student

moves.cueHe: המתן עד שיכנסו בעלי תריסין לבית המדרש
moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel defers the clash to the study hall.
moves.about: the Nasi defers the question until the scholars enter the study hall

moves.summary: The questioner rises and repeats the question before the assembly.
moves.about: whether the evening prayer is optional or obligatory, now asked publicly

moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel answers publicly: obligatory.
moves.about: the evening prayer is obligatory

moves.cueHe: כלום יש אדם שחולק בדבר זה?
moves.summary: He asks the Sages whether anyone disputes it — testing whether R' Yehoshua will stand by his view.
moves.about: whether anyone present disputes that the evening prayer is obligatory

moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel confronts him with the ruling reported in his own name.
moves.about: R' Yehoshua's public denial that anyone disputes contradicts the ruling reported in his own name

moves.summary: R' Yehoshua answers no, deferring to the Nasi rather than arguing publicly.
moves.about: no one disputes that the evening prayer is obligatory

moves.cueHe: יהושע, עמוד על רגליך ויעידו בך
moves.summary: He orders R' Yehoshua to stand while testimony is given against him.
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel orders R' Yehoshua to stand while testimony is given against him

moves.cueHe: עמד רבי יהושע על רגליו ואמר
moves.summary: R' Yehoshua concedes he issued the ruling: the living cannot contradict the living.
moves.about: R' Yehoshua admits he issued the ruling, since the living cannot contradict the living

moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel lectures while R' Yehoshua is left standing, until the assembly makes the disseminator stop.
moves.about: the assembly tells the disseminator to stop relaying Rabban Gamliel's lecture

moves.summary: Recalling two earlier afflictions, the assembly resolves to depose him.
moves.about: the assembly resolves to remove Rabban Gamliel from the office of Nasi

moves.summary: Whom shall we install in his place?
moves.about: whether to install R' Yehoshua as Nasi in Rabban Gamliel's place — rejected because he was party to the incident

moves.summary: R' Yehoshua is floated as the replacement.
moves.about: whether to install R' Akiva as Nasi — rejected because he lacks ancestral merit and might be divinely punished

moves.summary: Rejected: he was party to the incident, so his appointment would wound Rabban Gamliel most.
R' Akiva is floated.
Rejected: lacking ancestral merit, he would be vulnerable to Rabban Gamliel's resentment.

moves.cueHe: אלא נוקמיה לרבי אלעזר בן עזריה
moves.summary: They settle on R' Elazar ben Azarya — wise, rich, and tenth in descent from Ezra.
moves.about: R' Elazar ben Azarya is settled on as Nasi because he is wise, rich and tenth in descent from Ezra

moves.cueHe: הוא חכם — דאי מקשי ליה, מפרק ליה
moves.summary: Each of the three qualifications is unpacked in turn.
moves.about: whether he consents to become head of the yeshiva

moves.cueHe: אתו ואמרו ליה: ניחא ליה למר דליהוי ריש מתיבתא?
moves.summary: They ask him to accept the headship.
moves.about: he lays the offer of the office before his wife for her judgement

moves.cueHe: אמר להו: איזיל ואימליך באינשי ביתי
moves.summary: He will consult his household first, and goes to his wife.
moves.about: he will first consult his household

moves.summary: His wife objects that they may depose him as they deposed Rabban Gamliel.
moves.about: he should not take the office because they may depose him too

moves.cueHe: אמר לה: לשתמש אינש יומא חדא בכסא דמוקרא
moves.summary: Use the precious cup today; let it break tomorrow.
moves.about: one should take the opportunity that comes, even if it does not last

moves.summary: A second objection: he has no white hair and is too young to head the Sages.
moves.about: he is too young to head the Sages — he has no white hair

moves.cueHe: ההוא יומא בר תמני סרי שני הוה
moves.summary: He was eighteen that day; a miracle turned eighteen rows of his hair white.
moves.about: his own well-known formula, 'I am as one who is seventy years old'

moves.cueHe: היינו דקאמר רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
moves.summary: This is why he said 'as one who is seventy' and not 'seventy years old'.
moves.about: why he said 'like seventy years old' and not 'seventy years old' — he only looked far older than he was

moves.cueHe: תנא אותו היום, סלקוהו לשומר הפתח
moves.summary: A baraita: on that day the doorkeeper was removed and students were let in freely, reversing Rabban Gamliel's screening policy.
moves.about: what else changed in the study hall on the day of the deposition

moves.summary: Benches had to be added for the flood of new students.
moves.about: the dream of white jugs full of ashes was shown to Rabban Gamliel only to console him and does not mean the new students were worthless

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוחנן: פליגי בה אבא יוסף בן דוסתאי ורבנן
moves.summary: R' Yoḥanan reports a dispute over the number: four hundred benches or seven hundred.
moves.about: how many benches were added to the study hall that day

moves.cueHe: הוה קא חלשה דעתיה דרבן גמליאל
moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel is disheartened, fearing he had withheld Torah from Israel; a dream of ash-filled jugs answers him.
moves.about: how many benches were added to the study hall that day

moves.summary: The Gemara denies the dream's implication: it was shown only to console him.
Eduyyot was taught that day, and every 'on that day' refers to it; no pending halakha was left unresolved.
moves.about: tractate Eduyyot was taught on that day and every 'on that day' refers to it

moves.cueHe: ואף רבן גמליאל לא מנע עצמו מבית המדרש אפילו שעה אחת
moves.summary: Even Rabban Gamliel kept coming to the study hall, bearing no grudge.
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel held no grudge and did not absent himself from the study hall for even one moment

moves.cueHe: אמר להם: מה אני לבא בקהל?
moves.summary: Yehuda the Ammonite convert asks the study hall whether he may enter the congregation.
moves.about: whether an Ammonite convert may enter the congregation of Israel

moves.summary: A mishna is adduced to show Rabban Gamliel took part in that day's rulings.
moves.about: a mishna adduced to prove that Rabban Gamliel took part in that day's rulings

moves.cueHe: אמר לו רבן גמליאל: אסור אתה לבא בקהל
moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel forbids him.
moves.about: the convert is forbidden to enter the congregation

moves.cueHe: אמר לו רבי יהושע: מותר אתה לבא בקהל
moves.summary: R' Yehoshua permits him.
moves.about: the convert is permitted to enter the congregation

moves.cueHe: והלא כבר נאמר לא יבא עמוני ומואבי בקהל ה׳
moves.summary: He objects from Deuteronomy's explicit prohibition.
moves.about: the verse forbidding an Ammonite to enter the congregation refutes the permission R' Yehoshua gave

moves.cueHe: וכי עמון ומואב במקומן הן יושבין?
moves.summary: Sennacherib scrambled the nations, and whatever parts, parts from the majority.
moves.about: Sennacherib scrambled the nations, so the present inhabitants of Ammon are not ethnic Ammonites

moves.cueHe: והלא כבר נאמר ואחרי כן אשיב את שבות בני עמון
moves.summary: But Jeremiah promised Ammon's return, and they have already returned.
moves.about: Jeremiah's promise that Ammon's captivity would be restored means the original Ammonites have returned

moves.cueHe: והלא כבר נאמר ושבתי את שבות עמי ישראל
moves.summary: Israel's promised return is equally unfulfilled, so the prophecy proves nothing about the present.
moves.about: a parallel promise about Israel's return is also unfulfilled, so the prophecy proves nothing about the present

moves.summary: They immediately permit him — R' Yehoshua's view prevails, with Rabban Gamliel present.
moves.about: whether the Ammonite convert may enter the congregation — the study hall followed R' Yehoshua and permitted him

moves.cueHe: אמר רבן גמליאל: הואיל והכי הוה, איזיל ואפייסיה לרבי יהושע
moves.summary: Seeing the people follow R' Yehoshua, Rabban Gamliel goes to appease him.
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel goes to R' Yehoshua's house in order to appease him

moves.cueHe: מכותלי ביתך אתה ניכר שפחמי אתה
moves.summary: He remarks on the blackened walls, discovering R' Yehoshua's trade.
moves.about: remarking in wonderment that the blackened walls show R' Yehoshua to be a blacksmith

moves.summary: R' Yehoshua reproaches him for not knowing how Torah scholars live — an attack the text does not mark as any of the dialectical kinds.
moves.about: R' Yehoshua reproves Rabban Gamliel's conduct as Nasi for not knowing how Torah scholars make a living

moves.summary: He admits the insult and asks forgiveness.
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel admits he insulted him and asks his forgiveness

moves.summary: R' Yehoshua ignores him and does not forgive.
moves.about: R' Yehoshua accepts the apology and is appeased

moves.summary: He appeals to the honour of his father, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
moves.about: asking him to relent out of deference to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
